Subject: Realtime feed gaps during peak — multiple client timeouts

Hi Alex,

We started seeing a spike in WebSocket timeouts and partial chunk drops in our streaming inference sessions during our morning peak (approx 09:00–10:30 PT). Client-side logs show repeated 100-200ms gaps between chunks, then full disconnects at ~P99 for ~3% of requests. Overall latency (p99) jumped from ~450ms to >1.8s and error rate increased noticeably. This is impacting live features for our customers — two production incidents today so far.

Attached are a short pcap from one session (webrtc_pcap_0829.zip) and a snippet of client logs. Can we get immediate help? We're willing to join a war room.

On Sat, Aug 29, 2026 at 4:05 PM Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com> wrote:
> Alex — thanks for the signal and the captures. I'm escalating this now and standing up a short war room.

We reproduced a similar pattern against a replicated session in our staging cluster: bursts of small "blank" intervals between streamed chunks followed by client disconnects when cumulative idle crosses the client threshold. Initial findings:
- Root cause appears to be a coordination of three factors during bursts:
  1) edge proxy connection buffer re-ordering under high concurrent streams (not a full network drop, but chunk arrival jitter),
  2) our keepalive/idle window on the edge was too permissive and allowed the client to interpret gaps as a stalled stream,
  3) KV-cache evictions in the serving runtime when token sequences spike for a tenant, producing a short delay before the next chunk.
- Error rates correlate with increases in concurrent active sessions per GPU and a small regression in our streaming scheduler we pushed two days ago.

Immediate mitigations tested (quick smoke tests):
- Reduced edge idle threshold from 6s -> 1.5s (reduced observed disconnects in staging).
- Disabled an aggressive runtime GC hook that was firing on tenant burst; hold on rolling that hook out to prod until we complete analysis.
- Added stricter outbound chunk pacing (slightly coarser batching) to avoid re-ordering amplification.

I recommend a temporary routing policy for Geometrics traffic to a tuned pool (we can move them to a dedicated pool with conservative GC and extended prefetch) while we push a targeted runtime patch.

I'll attach the repro logs and a short trace.

—Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior SRE — Serving Runtime

Short summary: Geometrics is seeing P99 streaming latency and a small percentage of socket disconnects due to chunk arrival jitter + runtime cache thrashing during bursts. This started after our small scheduler change two days ago and is affecting their production customers (renewal conversation in Q4).

Ask: can we approve an immediate capacity/route change and a short SLA/credit for Geometrics while SRE pushes the patch? Recommended actions:
- Move Geometrics to a tuned dedicated pool (conservative GC, increased prefetch) for 72 hours to stabilize (low-risk config change).
- Apply the edge idle threshold rollback that reduced disconnects in staging (1.5s) across the edge for traffic from this tenant as a scoped policy.
- CS to offer a goodwill credit for the incident window and open a joint postmortem with Geometrics next week.

This will require ops capacity and a ratified temporary exception to our autoscaling policies. I'm happy to coordinate the change window; ask if we need exec sign-off.

—Alex

- Runtime GC hook is disabled for the tuned pool until the patch lands (planned patch: 9/2).
